Frigg, the queen of the Aesir and goddess of marriage, motherhood, home, and domestic life. She is the wife of Odin and one of the most powerful Aesir, possessing knowledge of the fates though she speaks them only rarely. Her wisdom rivals her husband's, but she embodies acceptance rather than intervention in the unfolding of destiny.

Frigg presides over Fensalir, her sacred hall, where she receives honored dead alongside Odin's warriors. Her maids and handmaidens carry out important tasks across the nine worlds, extending her influence far beyond Asgard itself. She represents the civilizing forces of home, family, and loyalty—a counterbalance to Odin's relentless quest for wisdom and war.

Her defining story centers on her desperate attempt to save her son Balder from a prophesied death. She binds all things with a solemn oath to spare him from harm, creating what she thought was absolute protection. But in her caution, she overlooked the mistletoe plant as too young and harmless. This tiny oversight became the loophole through which Loki struck, and Balder died. Her attempts to retrieve him from death failed, and her grief became legendary—all things wept for Balder's loss. Though she holds knowledge of future events just as Odin does, she could not prevent this tragedy, demonstrating the limits of even godly wisdom and maternal power against the threads the Norns have woven.
